title: Pipeline congestion simulator for mixed arrival profiles and p95 token slippage
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Goal: build a deterministic simulator and test harness that reproduces pipeline congestion modes seen in production when multiple arrival shapes (steady, bursty, chatty sessions) contend for batching and queueing resources. The harness will measure tokens/sec, server-side p95 token-emission latency, queue wait distributions, and regression detection against a stable baseline.

Motivation: past incidents showed that under heterogeneous tenant mixes the runtime's continuous batching heuristics amplify queueing delays for low-rate but high-length sessions. Existing harnesses focus on pure arrival profiles; we need a multi-profile, interleaved-signal harness that can (a) reproduce congestion hotspots, (b) surface p95 token slippage as a first-class metric, and (c) exercise fallback/routing policies to validate graceful degradation.

Scope: implement a simulator that can: generate labeled sessions with configurable arrival functions (Poisson, periodic microbursts, burst trains, user-interactive think-times), model KV prefix reuse probability, vary prompt/response token length distributions, and emulate multi-GPU routing with configurable batching windows and backpressure. Capture per-request token emission timestamps so p50/p95/p99 token latencies can be computed. Produce output artifacts: CSV/Parquet traces, Grafana-compatible metrics, synthetic load dashboard, and regression reports.

Non-goals: full integration with multi-tenant billing, exhaustive hardware kernel selection experiments, or UI for end users. This is an engineering harness for reproducible experiments and alerts integration.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a 1-hour mixed-profile job that contains at least three distinct arrival shapes and produces a trace with per-token emission timestamps
Measured baseline run (control) and experimental run differ in p95 token emission latency when congestion is injected; harness computes effect size and flags regressions > 15%
Exports metrics to the existing Grafana ingestion endpoint and provides a dashboard link with tokens/sec and p95 histograms
Regression detection pipeline (simple z-score + rolling-baseline) is wired to a test webhook that can create Linear issues when a regression is detected
All artifacts (raw traces, aggregated metrics, summary PDF) are uploaded to s3://redwood-benchmarks/pipeline-congestion/ENG-82456/ and linked from the ticket
tasks: Design simulator API and YAML job spec for arrival profiles
Implement arrival generator (Poisson, microburst, burst-train, interactive think-time)
Add token-emission instrumentation hooks to the runtime harness (timestamps per emitted token)
Model KV prefix hit-rate generator and integrate into session payloads
Implement queue/backpressure emulator that respects batching windows and per-GPU queue depth
Integrate metrics export (Prometheus pushgateway or push-compatible)
Build Grafana dashboard and template vars for quick comparisons
Write regression detection job and webhook to create Linear issues
Run baseline vs three perturbation scenarios and collect artifacts
Write docs + runbook for how to reproduce experiments and interpret reports
comments: 2025-11-02 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem #PM-7745 highlighted p95 token slippage during mixed tenant load. Initial scope drafted. Asked runtime team for instrumentation hooks.

2025-11-05 - Luis Romero: Architectural sync complete. Decided to keep simulator external to the serving binary; use a lightweight harness that calls the same request path as clients to exercise real routing and batching code paths. Will instrument at the point of token emission within the runtime agent.

2025-11-09 - Morgan Chen (review): Reviewed approach and requested we capture both per-request queuing time and per-token emission drift; suggested including an adaptive noise model to mimic network jitter. Agreed to add jitter param to the job spec.

2025-11-12 - Luis Romero: Prototype arrival generator implemented (poisson + microburst). Early run shows tokens/sec dips of ~22% at 95th percentile when 30% of sessions are long-chatty. Saved raw traces to s3://redwood-benchmarks/tmp/ENG-82456/run-20251112/

2025-11-15 - Asha Patel: Design review with Observability team. Decided to reuse existing Grafana folder runtime/perf/harnesses and create new dashboard 'pipeline-congestion' with p95 token emission and queue tail maps. Observability asked for taggable run IDs and sample-size annotations. Added to tasks.

2025-11-18 - Luis Romero: Implemented basic regression detector (rolling baseline mean + std). On controlled regression injection (increased long-chatty weight by 15%) detector fired with 18% p95 increase. Dashboard link: https://grafana.internal.redwood/runtime/perf/harnesses/pipeline-congestion?run=ENG-82456-20251118

2025-11-20 - Product feedback (Elena Morales): Useful for Dedicated capacity sizing; asked for a short summary PDF and a recommended set of workload mixes for dedicated capacity qualification. Added to acceptance criteria.
